missionPremise: Kit vendor-parity arm B is red for an INHERITED reason, not for anything any PR did. The dispatch asserted it and this lane WATCHED it failing on a pristine clone of kit main at 17eccfad before touching anything: SC_DASHBOARDS_DIR=P:/tmp/l2-dash npm test returned 86 tests / 85 pass / 1 fail / 0 skipped with arm B as the one failure. The blob table underneath it, taken committed-blob to committed-blob so no working tree and no CRLF question is involved, shows all four vendored files drifted from smartcity-dashboards main at fd52428d. PR #10's sc-kit.css is already correct at 3b89d4ae, exactly as the dispatch said, so the token file was never the problem. Refreshing the other three necessarily pulls G-93's two-source .prov, which the kit's Prov component could not express, and that is the card G-94 and G-98 both declined for the same stated reason. Sources: the compiled dispatch _dispatches/2026-08-20_l2_dispatch.md, amendment A-083 in 90_operations/OPS-17_govtech_stack_plan_of_record.md, the worked precedent _inbox/2026-08-19_t1kit_close.json which ran this same chain at G-90, and the product's own G-93 comment at web/index.html line 308, which states the rule the contract had to hold rather than this lane inventing one.
completionPredicate: A stranger can verify this without the executor. Clone smartcity-kit at PR #10's head 18d4234. Clone smartcity-dashboards at fd52428d. Run `npm run refresh:vendor -- <that dashboards checkout>` and see zero files change and the script print 'no upstream file changed'. Run `git hash-object vendor/<f>` for all four vendored files and get the same blob `git rev-parse HEAD:web/<f>` returns on the product side. Run the rule in test/_lib.mjs over the two vendored stylesheets and get 143, with vendor/sc-kit.css still at blob 3b89d4ae402dc974092950f1bbdcc1e5a96fbf7a. Run `SC_DASHBOARDS_DIR=<that checkout> npm test` and get 90 of 90 with nothing skipped, including the coverage assertion that every one of the 143 classes is emitted by some component. Run `npm run typecheck` and `npm run typecheck:examples` and get exit 0. Run `npm run prove:gates` and see 38 of 38 injections fire and name their file plus 1 of 1 control stay green. Read test/gate3-classes.test.mjs and find the coverage assertion unweakened, with no exclusion set and no class parked as structural. Read src/status.tsx and find ProvClaim.detail required and ProvProps a union whose two-claim arm makes detail required. Write `<Prov source="x" secondClaim={{ source: "y", detail: "z" }} />` in a consumer and watch the compiler reject it. Count exports of dist/index.mjs where typeof is function, GALLERY.length, and the files in .design-sync/previews, and get 86 from all three. The CI check-run conclusion string on 18d4234 is "success" and the run log contains `ok 89 - arm B`, `arm B ran`, `# tests 90 / # pass 90 / # fail 0 / # skipped 0`, `38 of 38 injected violations were caught and named`, and the upstream checkout line `fd52428d9a1f56b430feed6d9192ca336ed2378a`.
scopeBasis: The dispatch drew the boundary at a green PR and stopped short of the merge and of the DesignSync upload, both planner-owned, so neither is here. Inside that boundary the executable question was what the re-vendor turns red and what wrapping it requires, and the answer diverged from the planner's expectation in a way that decided the shape of the work: the COVERAGE assertion never went red, because the class vocabulary is 143 before and 143 after with zero added and zero removed, so there was nothing to wrap on that axis and no new component, gallery entry or preview is in this PR. What went red was markup parity, on two of twenty-two cases, and the two causes behind it are the two component CONTRACTS that changed. Deliberate exclusions, named rather than forgotten. vendor/sc-kit.css was not touched and did not move in the refresh, because a token change there is a product-line decision across three byte-locked repos and not a kit PR. ds-bundle/, .ds-sync/ and .render-check.json were not rebuilt or modified; none exists in a fresh clone, so nothing was wiped either. No case was added for a THIRD provenance claim or for a reordered interleave, because the product ships neither and a case with no product counterpart cannot fail for the right reason. test/_markup.mjs was NOT widened, because the nav-foot chip ships visible and the plain shapeAt rule applies to it. The example screens were corrected rather than gated, because examples/screens.tsx is a consumer composition and not a component. Two things were included beyond the literal ask and are named rather than buried: the State heading was held as a DIVERGENCE TEST against the vendored stylesheet rather than fixed with a one-token edit, because shell.css and surfaces.tsx are one rule with two implementations; and .design-sync/conventions.md gained a paragraph, because that file ships verbatim into the README uploaded to the Design project and its Provenance section would otherwise have told the design agent that a prov chip carries one figure while the product ships two.

provContractChange.whatTheComponentNOWexpresses: a discriminated union on the props. Arm one is the previous component unchanged: source required, detail optional, which is the form eleven shipped single-figure chips take. Arm two adds secondClaim, a ProvClaim pair of source and detail where BOTH are required, and makes the top-level detail required. The emitted order is b source, sep, b secondClaim.source, sep, detail, sep, secondClaim.detail, which is byte-for-byte the product's order.
whatItREFUSES: a second figure with no counting rule of its own. ProvClaim.detail is not optional.
a second figure while the FIRST has no counting rule. detail is required on the two-claim arm, so <Prov source secondClaim> does not compile.
a third claim. There is no prop for one and the product ships none, so a case built on it could never fail for the right reason.
reordering the interleave. The order is emitted by the component and is not a prop.
whatItDOESNOTrefuse_statedRatherThanOmit: a single-figure chip with no detail. Eleven shipped instances are bold-only LABELS rather than figures, so requiring a rule on every bold slot would make the shipped form unrepresentable.

any consistency check between the two figures. A React component cannot type-check the relationship between two values, and DEV_PROCESS rule 0 says a control that depends on someone remembering is not a control.
a basis line inside the chip. Prov has no basis slot and the product puts none there.

theOneRealDesignDecision.question: the shipped chip groups the two figures at the head and the two rules at the tail. A claims array reads as figure, rule, figure, rule.
theOneRealDesignDecision.chosen: secondClaim, a single optional pair, with the interleave emitted by the component.
theOneRealDesignDecision.why: an array would have either rendered markup the product does not have or needed a silent reordering step inside the component, and src/status.tsx already states the governing rule in its own words: wrapping would make the component render markup the product does not have, which is the one thing a wrapper must never do. It would also have made N claims representable when the product ships at most two.
theOneRealDesignDecision.cost: the reading order of the props is not the reading order of the output, which is a real trap. Named in the component doc, and held by the order test, the parity case and an injection rather than by the comment.
theOneRealDesignDecision.whatWasNotDone: no runtime check that the two figures are about the same subject, and no attempt to make a third claim a compile error with a custom message. The first is not expressible in a React component and the second would be a message nobody reads; the union simply has no third arm.

THE COVERAGE ASSERTION IS NOT THE ONLY DETECTOR, AND THIS ROW SHOWED WHY. The brief assumed a re-vendor's work list comes from the coverage gate going red. It did not move at all, and the real work list came from markup parity. A product change that alters ELEMENTS, ids or selector shape rather than classes is invisible to gate 3 by construction. The State h5 sat wrong in the kit from G-95 until this lane, and the only thing that caught it was a parity case that happens to exist for one screen. Worth a row: an element-level divergence test for every component whose stylesheet rule is element-scoped, not just for .state.

A TYPE THAT GETS WEAKER IS INVISIBLE TO A LAW TEST. Recorded above in full. Any future kit law expressed at the TYPE needs its injection aimed at test/consumer.test.mjs, and a law test reading source strings will score green on a relaxed optionality. This is a general rule for this repo and not a one-off.
